races.name: ROA/RSA Shared Ownership Day Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tellherthename
runners_data.note: OR 138 with recent Goodwood wins over good ground and a 17-day turnaround suits; Dan Skelton's yard is firing (14/28 over 14 days) and this horse's natural pace makes it the controlling force, though it is running somewhat out of role as a confirmed front-runner rather than pure prominent racer — style fit (0.93) is high but worth noting.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with four wins or places in last five runs, all at 16-17f on good ground, gives it genuine claims; Jennie Candlish sends it out fresh (23 days) with tongue-tie fitted, and the 3lb claim from Luke Scott is a tangible weight advantage in a tight three-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies's runner has mixed recent form (P and 2 in last two), and the trainer's 0/5 14-day record gives little confidence; naturally a prominent type, it appears in a hold-up position here purely because the field has no genuine back-markers, and its style fit (0.87) suggests it will not truly race from off the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Tellherthename is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only three runners in a small field, will stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and control every yard of this 2m1f chase on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Captain Cool and Ice In The Veins are both natural prominent-racing types, meaning none of the three will be content to truly sit off the pace — but with Tellherthename the most committed pace-setter, the other two will likely track closely rather than mount a serious challenge for the lead from the start. The result is an unhurried, single-file procession at a sustainable tempo, with minimal pressure on the leader and the race likely to be decided by jumping quality and finishing stamina in the home straight. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or patient prominent types who can conserve energy and produce a late challenge — though with all three runners being natural front or prominent types, Tellherthename's ability to dictate an uncontested lead gives it a significant tactical edge, while Ice In The Veins has been redistributed to a hold-up role only because the field lacks any true back-markers, and it is not a natural closer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tellherthename Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tellherthename bowls along in front at a controlled tempo and neither rival has the means to reel it in late.
scenarios.body: If Tellherthename bowls along in front at a controlled tempo and neither rival has the means to reel it in late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Captain Cool Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool, with its strong recent form record (four wins and places in last five), tracks Tellherthename throughout and outstays it from the final fence.
scenarios.body: If Captain Cool, with its strong recent form record (four wins and places in last five), tracks Tellherthename throughout and outstays it from the final fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Tellherthename sets a pace that proves unsustainable on the quick ground and weakens after the last, leaving the race open.
scenarios.body: If Tellherthename sets a pace that proves unsustainable on the quick ground and weakens after the last, leaving the race open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Disrupt Order
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping mistake or unseating by the leader mid-race reshuffles the running order entirely.
scenarios.body: If a jumping mistake or unseating by the leader mid-race reshuffles the running order entirely.

watchPoints.text: Tellherthename's jumping must be monitored — if it makes a mid-race error on good-to-firm ground it hands control directly to Captain Cool, who is the main threat on recent form.

Ice In The Veins is not a natural hold-up horse and will likely be drawn into tracking the pace, meaning its mapped position is misleading and punters should not rely on it producing a late run from the rear.
Captain Cool's 3lb claim from Luke Scott (3) could be influential in a tight finish — inexperienced conditional jockeys in small-field chases can be a variable, particularly under pressure at fences.

Good-to-firm going at Stratford is confirmed across all races this card; all three runners show OK going preference, but Tellherthename's best form comes on good ground and the conditions suit it directly.

With only three runners, there is no hiding place tactically — any horse that loses its position at an early fence will find it very difficult to recover ground in what shapes up as a single-file, strung-out contest.

races.name: Racehorse Ownership From 25 Pound At racingclub.com Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Colibri Bleu
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo who showed placed form over 2m on Good going wearing headgear, and the hg:h flag is worth noting as a potential concentration aid; Jack Andrews takes the ride for Tim Ellis whose 14-day figures are solid, and two runs at this trip in similar conditions provide a small but relevant sample, though the PP-P37 form string points to inconsistency.|

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Placed form in 2020/21 is very stale — recent return showing a fourth at 2m on Good (16f) is the only truly current reference point; Stan Sheppard partners for Matt Sheppard with a blank 14-day book suggesting no recent momentum, and the 27-day freshen could be either positive or negative for a horse with an erratic form profile.|

runners_data.name: King Troy
runners_data.note: Long 479-day absence is a serious fitness concern and the form string of P0/P-U reflects a jumps career that has struggled for fluency; Alison Thorpe sends this 7yo out from a yard with 0/5 in the 14-day window, and while the horse is a natural hold-up type, the redistribution to midfield means it will race closer than ideal, compounding the fitness worry.|

runners_data.name: Mr Rafiki
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — three consecutive fourths including in 16f and 20f Good-ground events — and Jonjo O'Neill Jr is a strong jockey booking for a yard with reasonable activity; a genuine hold-up horse by style, he is plotted in midfield here because there are too many closers for the map to accommodate at the rear, meaning his race will be run further forward than the trainer would ideally want.|

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: Irish-trained 6yo sent over by John Joseph Hanlon, whose 14-day record of 0/22 is poor, and Paddy Hanlon takes the 5lb claim; best form includes a second at 12f on Standard (AW) and a third at 18f on Good, suggesting stamina is not an issue but the horse is a natural hold-up type racing in a field that pushes him into a position he won't naturally find.|

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Five consecutive hurdles runs on Good or Good-to-Soft, best of which is a second at 2m on Soft, giving a consistent but winless profile; Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell claims 7lb which is valuable, and the horse's authentic hold-up style means it is correctly mapped without redistribution — a genuine closer who needs the pace set by Bound For Glory to be strong enough for this profile to land.|

runners_data.name: Bound For Glory
runners_data.note: Won last time at Hereford (2m, Good) and is the only genuine front-runner here; Ciaran Gethings should secure a frictionless lead with zero pressure expected, though the step to 2m2½f on Good to Firm is the one unknown — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this horse may not be a natural front-runner at the highest level, but conditions clearly suit.|

runners_data.name: Square d'Alboni
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 14-day strike rate of 21/78 is the strongest trainer angle in the race, and Harry Skelton is a potent booking at any course; a natural hold-up horse on form (3rd in 16f Soft most recently), the step to Good to Firm and 2m2½f is untested but the pedigree and trainer form suggest this 4yo is likely to be better than its current form figures show.|

races.paceDynamic: Bound For Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner maiden hurdle, and with no other genuine pace-setter to push them, Ciaran Gethings can dictate proceedings at whatever tempo suits over 2m2½f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. The redistribution note is significant here: Penzance, Mr Rafiki, and King Troy are all natural hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded with similar types — none of them are likely to pressure Bound For Glory early, reinforcing an uncontested lead. This creates a sustainable, controlled gallop with Bound For Glory able to conserve energy jumping, dictating margin and tempo through the middle stages, and potentially sprinting clear from the home turn. The race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead types who travel fluently and stay the trip, with closers carrying an inherent risk of finding too much ground to make up on a front-runner that is never harassed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bound For Glory Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bound For Glory leads comfortably from the outset and no rival has the pace or inclination to close the gap mid-race.
scenarios.body: If Bound For Glory leads comfortably from the outset and no rival has the pace or inclination to close the gap mid-race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bound For Glory sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field, leaving space for a finisher to pick them off at the last.
scenarios.body: If Bound For Glory sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field, leaving space for a finisher to pick them off at the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Sprint Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and runners begin to close on Bound For Glory, triggering a sprint from the second-last.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses mid-race and runners begin to close on Bound For Glory, triggering a sprint from the second-last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Field Fragments
scenarios.trigger: If the field breaks into distinct groups with several horses jumping poorly or losing positions, creating a ragged race shape.
scenarios.body: If the field breaks into distinct groups with several horses jumping poorly or losing positions, creating a ragged race shape.

watchPoints.text: Bound For Glory leads absolutely uncontested — if Gethings gets away cleanly at the first and no rival shows any interest in tracking closely, watch for this horse to open up a gap from the home turn that the hold-up field cannot close.

King Troy's 479-day layoff combined with a history of falls and unseats (U in form string) makes this runner a jumping-safety concern — any loose horse or sprawling jump could compromise the chances of horses directly behind, particularly Mr Rafiki and Penzance who will be racing in the same midfield band.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (King Troy, Mr Rafiki, Penzance) all racing closer than their natural style suggests creates a congested midfield — watch for crowding or interference at the early hurdles as these runners fail to settle into their preferred positions.

Square d'Alboni represents the Skelton yard whose 14-day record (21/78) is the standout trainer angle; if Harry Skelton moves him into second or third tracking Bound For Glory from the third-last, that is a significant position shift worth monitoring as a market mover justification.

Usyk, the only undisturbed genuine hold-up horse alongside Square d'Alboni, will give a clear read on whether the pace Bound For Glory sets is fast enough to bring closers into it — if Usyk is still last and detached at halfway, the pace is too slow for hold-up types to win.

races.name: SolidCAM UK Partner Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jamie Snowden, in fine form (won two of last four on good ground at this trip), tongue-tie fitted, returns after 33 days and sets the entire tempo here — his natural style gives him a structural advantage but his OR of 115 and last run sixth may tempt rivals to close him down late.

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's six-year-old has solid prominent form on good ground (8/8 sim-going record), ridden by the trainer's conditional Fern O'Brien, and the step up to 2m6f is the main question given all five recent runs have been at shorter — positional comfort means she travels well here if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Balboa
runners_data.note: Seamus Mullins runner whose best recent effort came winning over 2m on soft, but the overall record at this trip and on good ground is thin (0W1P in 15 similar runs), and as a natural prominent who may get shuffled back in a crowded early lead, his chance depends heavily on securing a clean run.

runners_data.name: Tyson
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse handled expertly by Harry Skelton, and his most recent run — a second over 2m6f on good — confirms both the trip and going suit; he is the most credible closer in the field but needs the pace to quicken or collapse to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Prince De Juilley
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a fine place record in similar conditions (12/15 sim-going, 6 places) for Alastair Ralph; by inclination a front-runner, he will need to settle for a tracking role rather than his preferred lead, which historically he manages — headgear (p) suggests he needs restraining — and he is capable if the scenario plays to him.

runners_data.name: Lion Of The Desert
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's six-year-old has genuine prominent tendencies but will be pushed into a midfield role by the congestion up front; the horse has an excellent sim-going record (9/15, 2W4P) and handles good ground well, so if he travels smoothly in the pack rather than fretting at his displaced position, he remains a live outsider.

runners_data.name: The Gypsy Davey
runners_data.note: Mrs C Williams sends out an eight-year-old amateur-ridden (7lb claimer B T Stone) who has not won in five attempts at this going band recently (sim-going 14/15, 0 wins in last five) and is trained with no winner in 14 days; last run was 56 days ago, and the combination of weak pace suitability, amateur pilot, and flat recent form makes him the least threatening of the hold-up horses.

runners_data.name: Minella Double
runners_data.note: Rob Summers's eight-year-old is a natural hold-up horse returning after a 130-day break with no 14-day trainer strike rate and a form string featuring two pulls-up recently — the long absence is a significant concern, and while there is a placed run on good ground in his history, he needs everything to fall right after such a layoff.

races.paceDynamic: Jackstell is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing or able to dispute the lead, he will control tempo from the outset over this 2m6f trip on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Prince De Juilley, Lion Of The Desert, and Balboa are all natural prominent types but the field cannot accommodate them all in their preferred position — Prince De Juilley and Lion Of The Desert are most likely to secure a berth close to Jackstell, while Balboa may find himself squeezed back from his natural spot. With Jackstell dictating an uncontested, sustainable gallop, the race is unlikely to turn into a genuine stamina test; instead, it sets up as a positional race where those racing prominently or just off the pace in a smooth rhythm have a structural advantage over hold-up horses who will face a flat, unaccelerated finish with little cover from the pace. The clear tactical verdict is that prominent racers and horses comfortable travelling close to the leader are favoured — true hold-up horses who must make up ground late will find the race shape working against them on this relatively flat, right-handed track with a steady pace set by a single front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackstell Controls, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jackstell sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent horses travelling just behind him have enough in reserve to challenge from 2 out.
scenarios.body: If Jackstell sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent horses travelling just behind him have enough in reserve to challenge from 2 out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jackstell Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Jackstell's uncontested lead and strong recent form allow him to steal an unassailable advantage from the front that the others cannot close down.
scenarios.body: If Jackstell's uncontested lead and strong recent form allow him to steal an unassailable advantage from the front that the others cannot close down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the front two or three fade, allowing Tyson or The Gypsy Davey to close from further back.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens mid-race and the front two or three fade, allowing Tyson or The Gypsy Davey to close from further back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Prominent War
scenarios.trigger: If Balboa and Lion Of The Desert both push to the fore early and press Jackstell hard, turning the race into a genuine slog that plays into the hands of a fresh hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: If Balboa and Lion Of The Desert both push to the fore early and press Jackstell hard, turning the race into a genuine slog that plays into the hands of a fresh hold-up horse.

watchPoints.text: Jackstell (Gavin Sheehan) — watch whether he is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the early stages; if he steals 4-5 lengths before the field reacts, the race could be effectively over before the third flight.

Prince De Juilley and Lion Of The Desert — both are natural front-runners squeezed into mid-pack roles; if either becomes unsettled and expends energy fighting for position in the first mile, their chance is compromised before the race begins.

Tyson (Harry Skelton) — watch his position jumping the last before the home turn; if he is more than six lengths off the pace at that point with no acceleration in the pace ahead, his hold-up style leaves him with too much to do on this flat track.

Minella Double — returning from 130 days off with no recent trainer form, this runner's jumping accuracy and manageability in the early stages should be monitored; a sloppy first flight could confirm he is not wound up enough to threaten.

Going note — official going is Good To Firm for this race (confirmed by the going report), which plays to horses with sound records on a quick surface and may put extra emphasis on jumping fluency over the 2m6f trip.

races.name: Davisons Law Moving You Forward Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Zhang Fei
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for in-form Fergal O'Brien, who sends out Fern O'Brien (5lb claimer) — good to firm record is acceptable (11/15) but the horse's last five runs show no wins at similar trips and the pace map puts genuine closers like this at a disadvantage today.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and pace-maker with a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting this prominent role is outside his absolute comfort zone; nevertheless he is the only horse prepared to lead and on a 9-day turnaround, connections will likely let him bowl along and use that position aggressively.

runners_data.name: Get The Value
runners_data.note: John O'Shea's veteran hold-up type has a poor recent form string (8P7-7P) and, while going is fine, the lack of a recent strong finish and a modest trainer 14-day record of 1/6 make it hard to see him winning from the back of this field.

runners_data.name: Charlie My Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent staying hold-up horse with an outstanding record on good ground (14/15, three wins) and the trip suits — James Davies takes the ride for a trainer who has one win from six in 14 days, so the each-way angle is stronger than the win case given today's pace shape.

runners_data.name: Western Soldier
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in reality, pushed into a midfield mapping because of the congestion of closers; Callum Pritchard rides for Seamus Mullins but a going record of only 7/15 on good and inconsistent recent form (U, 4, 5) tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Katzoff
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride, which is the headline — but this is a true rear-of-field type whose form figures (9, 0, P, 2, 6) are patchy and whose last win came over a shorter trip; the midfield mapping overstates his likely position in running today.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old hold-up type for Barry John Murphy, displaced into midfield by field congestion; only 7/11 on good going and a modest OR of 79 means this horse is swimming against the tactical tide in a race shaped for the front two.

runners_data.name: Stellarmasterpiece
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this hood-wearing prominent racer for Micky Hammond, whose T14 strike rate of 3/19 is solid — last win was at 16f on good and the horse is the only credible market rival to Newport for tracking the pace from the off.

runners_data.name: Winston's Oath
runners_data.note: Four-year-old on just 4/8 good-going runs with no wins, trained by Dylan Cunha whose T14 reads 1/30; a true hold-up horse mapped into midfield through congestion, which understates how far back this one will actually race.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby have the best trainer 14-day figures in the field (5/34) but Brooklyn Lullaby's form (6U07-5) is poor and the horse has never made the frame at today's course-distance combination — a natural closer who will find this pace shape unkind.

races.paceDynamic: Newport is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, will coast into a comfortable lead and set a measured, controlled gallop on good to firm ground over 2m2½f. Stellarmasterpiece is the one horse likely to sit in closest pursuit from a prominent position, but neither she nor anyone else appears set to challenge Newport for that early berth, meaning the tempo will be honest rather than searching. The hold-up brigade — Zhang Fei, Charlie My Boy, Get The Value and others — will need Newport to do enough in front to wind the race up sufficiently for late challenges to land, which on this going is not guaranteed if Newport's connections allow him to dictate fully on his own terms. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a single uncontested pace-setter on a flat, turning track in good to firm conditions creates a significant tactical advantage for Newport and, to a lesser degree, Stellarmasterpiece. Several runners — Western Soldier, Winston's Oath, Katzoff, Yanka Blue and Brooklyn Lullaby — are genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield because there are simply too many closers for the map to accommodate at the rear; of these, Western Soldier and Katzoff, who have the most experience in this type of contest, are best placed to secure the most forward of those redistributed positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Newport Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Newport is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a sustainable but race-winning gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: If Newport is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a sustainable but race-winning gallop from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Stellarmasterpiece travels prominently behind Newport and Newport weakens late, allowing her to hit the front and sustain the run home.
scenarios.body: If Stellarmasterpiece travels prominently behind Newport and Newport weakens late, allowing her to hit the front and sustain the run home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Newport sets a stronger pace than anticipated and the hold-up horses get a proper target to aim at from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Newport sets a stronger pace than anticipated and the hold-up horses get a proper target to aim at from the home turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Gifts Result
scenarios.trigger: If Newport is taken on early or makes a jumping error and the race falls apart tactically, producing a messy, attritional finish.
scenarios.body: If Newport is taken on early or makes a jumping error and the race falls apart tactically, producing a messy, attritional finish.

watchPoints.text: Newport's jumping accuracy at the first two hurdles will be critical — if he stumbles or is headed early, the entire race shape collapses and the hold-up runners inherit a genuinely contested contest.

Stellarmasterpiece is fitted with a hood for the first time today (headgear flag: p); if the hood sharps her up she could apply unexpected pressure on Newport from the second hurdle, transforming this from a solo lead into a contested pace.

Charlie My Boy is the most credible hold-up threat based on going form (14/15) but needs Newport to either quicken the pace or tire — watch how far back James Davies positions him early, as dropping too far in a 10-runner field on a flat track can prove fatal.

Harry Skelton on Katzoff is worth monitoring at the start — Skelton will likely push for a forward position despite the horse's natural style, and if he secures a prominent pitch it upgrades Katzoff's chance materially versus the mapped scenario.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm across all six races at Stratford today, confirming a fast, true surface — premium on horses who travel fluently rather than those requiring cut, which reinforces the advantage to Newport and Stellarmasterpiece throughout.

races.name: Laura Horsfall Racing Club Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lady Kara
runners_data.note: Five wins from her last six starts including four on good ground at 17-20f make her an obvious pace angle here; she leads from the front and will be uncontested, but her OR of 112 means she is giving weight to everyone and the handicapper is catching up — her style suits this perfectly though headgear (hood/tongue-tie) is consistent with previous runs.

runners_data.name: Therhythmofthenite
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning recently (four places from last four runs), he races prominently and Tom Cannon provides a good jockey booking, but his form at 23f on heavier ground and only two runs in similar going (0 wins) raises a fitness and surface question on this quicker surface.

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: An 8yo whose best recent run was a second at 17f on good ground, he races from hold-up and trainer John Joseph Hanlon's yard is in excellent current form (T14: 2/31); the 5lb claim from Paddy Hanlon adds interest, though his recent form string of 9F-527 shows inconsistency jumping chasers.

runners_data.name: Delpotro
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen, one of the shrewdest tactical jockeys in the sport, takes over on this hold-up performer who has placed on four of his last five starts including two seconds at 16-21f on good ground; his sim-going record of 2W6P from 14 runs confirms he handles these conditions well, and the 31-day break is not a concern given Charlie Longsdon's record freshening horses.

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins (most recently at 24f on good ground) show strong current form for Dan Skelton's yard, which is firing at 8/23 over 14 days; his true racing style is hold-up and he has been pushed into midfield on the map due to multiple closers in this small field — his winning chance depends on finding clear air from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner — if he does run, he is a genuine hold-up horse with a win at 21f and multiple placed efforts, and Dan Skelton's yard is clearly in form; like Glenmalure Flyer, his natural closing style is cramped by the field composition, and the tongue-piece (tp headgear) plus only 11 days since last run are factors to weigh carefully.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Kara is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a six-runner field, she can dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front over this 2m3½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Therhythmofthenite carries prominent-horse credentials but has not shown the speed or inclination to take Lady Kara on for the early lead, meaning the pace is almost certain to be Lady Kara's to set as she pleases. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Glenmalure Flyer and Thickthorn Tom are genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield slots because the pace picture leaves no room for multiple true hold-up horses to operate from their natural position. A single, uncontested pace-setter on a flat, galloping track in good-to-firm conditions strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners with proven finishing kicks, provided they can bridge the gap Lady Kara will control from in front — but with so many closers compressed into midfield, the tactical edge belongs to the horse with the best cruising speed and jumping accuracy to track Lady Kara without expending early energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Kara Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kara leads from flag to finish at a measured gallop and no runner has the pace or inclination to close her down.
scenarios.body: If Lady Kara leads from flag to finish at a measured gallop and no runner has the pace or inclination to close her down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Lands Killer Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kara's lead is sustainable early but a genuine closer produces a powerful late run over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: If Lady Kara's lead is sustainable early but a genuine closer produces a powerful late run over the final two fences.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Rival Applies Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Therhythmofthenite or another prominent type pushes forward early and forces Lady Kara into a faster-than-intended pace.
scenarios.body: If Therhythmofthenite or another prominent type pushes forward early and forces Lady Kara into a faster-than-intended pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and horses forced back from their natural hold-up positions manage to rebalance and produce a genuine finishing run.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final mile and horses forced back from their natural hold-up positions manage to rebalance and produce a genuine finishing run.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kara's uncontested lead at a controlled pace over fences on good-to-firm ground at Stratford is the biggest tactical advantage in the race — watch how quickly she establishes that lead from the off and whether Therhythmofthenite attempts to go with her early.

Glenmalure Flyer and Thickthorn Tom are both genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by the race shape — if they get blocked or fail to find gaps approaching the final two fences, their finishing runs will be compromised regardless of form.

Delpotro has Sean Bowen in the saddle and a consistent placed record at this trip and going, but watch whether he can close a controlled gap set by Lady Kara — a slow early pace reduces his finishing kick window significantly.

The going for this race is Good to Firm (reported as Good on the racecard but confirmed Good to Firm by the going report) — Lady Kara's sim-going record of 10/11 on similar ground is the standout stat in the field and flags her as the primary pace-shape beneficiary.

Thickthorn Tom is listed as a non-runner — if confirmed absent, the field drops to five and the pace dynamic becomes even more uncontested for Lady Kara, further compressing the midfield and making Delpotro's hold-up role slightly easier to execute with one fewer rival in his path.
